scraped_articles.title: Centre seeks Punjab govt report on activist Jhota’s murder, measures to prevent drug trafficking
scraped_articles.content:
The Centre has sought a report from the Punjab government on the killing of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh, alias Jhota, and the steps taken to strengthen the state's anti-narcotics operations.
The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has asked the state government to submit a detailed account of the October 13 killing in Mansa, PTI reported. It has also sought details of measures taken to combat drug trafficking and substance abuse.
The MHA has called for the implementation of key measures to support the national goal of a drug-free India. These include setting up a dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), conducting financial investigations in drug-related cases and strengthening prosecution under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.
The ministry has also stressed the need for better coordination through the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism. Other priorities include designating special NDPS courts, appointing nodal officers and taking action against transnational drug networks.
Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight in Mansa on October 13 during a confrontation at a medical store over the alleged sale of addictive substances. He had been campaigning against drug abuse and the alleged illegal sale of habit-forming medicines at chemist shops.
Jhota was known for confronting suspected sellers and recording videos of such encounters for social media, according to reports.
On the day of the incident, he and his associates allegedly confronted a medical store owner over the sale of addictive drugs. The confrontation reportedly turned violent, with the shop owner allegedly opening fire. Jhota was killed, while others were injured.
The killing triggered protests in Mansa and other parts of Punjab. Jhota's family refused to cremate his body and demanded action against those responsible. His supporters and several farmer organisations also called for a statewide bandh on October 16.
Opposition parties and farmer groups backed demands for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe.
Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh and Congress MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring criticised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the state's law-and-order situation and its handling of the drug menace.
Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon demanded a CBI probe into Jhota's killing, while Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia called for the dissolution of the state government and the imposition of President's Rule.

scraped_articles.title: India urges US to ensure safety of its citizens after alleged plot to target Hindu temple in Illinois
scraped_articles.content:
India on Friday called on the United States to ensure the safety and security of Indian nationals after authorities foiled an alleged mass-shooting plot at a Hindu temple in Illinois. The suspect, a teenager, expressed violent “anti-Indian and white supremacist” views, investigators claimed.
The alleged plot was a “matter of deep concern for us”, ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Friday. He urged US authorities to take necessary steps to protect the Indian community.
“We have seen reports about an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting targeting a Hindu temple in Illinois. This is a matter of deep concern for us,” Jaiswal said.
He added that India took note of the action taken by US law enforcement agencies in the case and called on the American side to ensure the “safety and security of Indian nationals” in the country.
ALSO READ | Surrounded by 4 cops, cuffed on the ground: Video shows arrest of US teen accused of plotting Hindu temple shooting
Nineteen-year-old Alexandros Paporakis was arrested in Palatine, a suburb of Chicago, on October 11 over an alleged plot to attack a Hindu temple. Police launched an investigation after his co-workers alerted them to disturbing text messages.
Investigators allege that Paporakis planned to target Indians at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Temple in Aurora, located about 65 km west of downtown Chicago. He focused on the temple for around two months, according to prosecutors.
Prosecutors also alleged that Paporakis attempted to carry out the attack on October 11 but his rifle malfunctioned when he tried to shoot a man from a car.
According to prosecutors, he had told colleagues that he “couldn't wait to kill Indian people” and referred to Sunday as the “special day”.
ALSO READ | Alexandros Paporakis: Inside chilling manifesto of teen accused of plotting mass shooting at Hindu temple in Aurora
Investigators recovered a document attributed to Paporakis titled “Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)”. The document contained white supremacist and extremist ideologies, including references to violence against people of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian origin, according to police.
In the manifesto, Paporakis described himself as “a sociopathic white supremacist Neo Nazi filled with hatred, fantasising about mass murder nearly every day”, according to court records cited by the Chicago Sun-Times.
The document reportedly outlined his alleged plan for mass violence and expressed hostility towards minority communities, including Indian, Jewish and African-American people.
ALSO READ | How US teen’s Hindu temple attack plot was foiled: Rifle jam, online search, call to co-worker
A search of his residence led to the recovery of a rifle, multiple loaded rifle magazines, hundreds of rounds of ammunition and a tactical vest containing body armour. Police also recovered a patch displaying imagery associated with white supremacist extremism.
Authorities have said that, based on their investigation so far, Paporakis appeared to have been acting alone. The investigation remains ongoing
The teenager has been charged with making a terrorist threat, a Class X felony, and illegal possession of weapons. He was ordered to remain in custody following a court hearing and is due to appear in court again on October 30.
On Thursday, the MEA called the alleged plot a “racist, anti-Hindu attack” and asked American authorities to thoroughly investigate the matter and bring those responsible to justice.
ALSO READ | 'Racist hostility', 'anti-India hate': India on 'attempted mass shooting' targeting Hindu temple in US
“We are deeply concerned by reports of an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting targeting a Hindu temple in the Aurora area of Illinois. The reported anti-Hindu and racist nature of the alleged plot, including references to violence against people of Indian origin, is particularly disturbing,” Jaiswal said in response to media queries.
“We expect US authorities to thoroughly investigate the matter, bring those responsible to justice, and take all necessary measures to prevent such incidents.”
The incident, he said, added to “growing concerns over racist hostility and anti-India hate in the US”. “There is a need for greater vigilance, zero tolerance for hate-motivated violence, and decisive action to ensure the safety and security of the Indian community,” Jaiswal added.

scraped_articles.title: HT Evening Brief October 16: Abhijeet Dipke detained ahead of Delhi march; police deny claims of Dhruv Rathee's arrest
scraped_articles.content:
Good evening! Here's your 5-minute wrap of the day's top headlines from across the country and the world.
Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was detained by Delhi Police on Friday while he was heading to Connaught Place to participate in the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' event. The event was scheduled to be held at 5 pm on October 16. Delhi Police had urged Dipke to call off the gathering, citing concerns over traffic disruption, public safety and the inconvenience it could cause to traders and commuters. Read more here .
Police in Uttar Pradesh's Noida on Friday refuted social media claims alleging the arrest of Germany-based YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, describing the information as completely false, misleading and baseless. Notably, since Friday morning, several users have been posting on X, speculating that Dhruv Rathee was arrested by Noida Police and sharing a video to support the claim. Read more here .
Booth-level officers (BLOs) in Delhi have been directed to carry out a reverification of over 47 lakh voters whose names were removed from the draft electoral rolls, to ensure that no eligible voter is left out in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Ashok Kumar said on Friday. Read more here .
Marathi thriller Gondhal is heading to theatres across India on November 13, after being selected as India's official entry for the 99th Academy Awards in the Best International Feature Film category. The Film Federation of India (FFI) announced the selection on September 18, bringing the film national attention ahead of its theatrical release. Read more here .
Ever since the BCCI made it mandatory for its cricketers to participate in domestic cricket, the Ranji Trophy has regained some of its lost star power. Last season saw Virat Kohli turn out for Delhi in whites for the first time in 13 years, while Rohit Sharma also played a game for Mumbai after nearly a decade. Read more here .

scraped_articles.title: Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora detained by Delhi Police amid CJP's protest call
scraped_articles.content:
Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and student leader Neha Bora have been detained by the Delhi Police. Dipke was detained while he was heading to Connaught Place to participate in the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' event, while Bora was detained just when she began her march from Mandi House. Track live updates on Delhi protest
The event was scheduled to be held at 5 pm on October 16. Delhi Police had urged Dipke to call off the gathering , citing concerns over traffic disruption, public safety and the inconvenience it could cause to traders and commuters.
Track LIVE updates from CJP protest
Dipke stepped out of the house where he was staying and walked towards the street, where police personnel stopped him. After a brief exchange, the officers drove him away in a police vehicle.
In an exchange with police personnel, shared by ANI, a police official could be heard telling Dipke that he was being taken into preventive detention, citing the prohibitory order under Section 163 in force in Connaught Place.
Dipke, however, argued that he had not violated any law and asked the police to suggest an alternative venue for the event.
Also Read | Dhruv Rathee not arrested: Noida Police calls social media posts on YouTuber false
The CJP founder had called for a ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ event at Central Park in Connaught Place to protest the arrests of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. The CJP leaders were arrested after allegedly breaching barricades at Jantar Mantar following the Centre’s decision to denotify the protest site. Both Das and Ranka have been judicial custody since then.
The row had begun with the CJP and Opposition groups demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the conduct of elections in India and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The CJP’s October 10 plan to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was thwarted by Delhi Police, with founder Abhijit Dipke and members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka detained.
However, INDIA bloc MPs led by Rahul Gandhi held a rally towards the Supreme Court to submit a petition against the CEC.
Dipke, Das and Ranka were later released by a court. The Centre subsequently denotified Jantar Mantar as a protest site. Das, Ranka and other CJP members later gathered at Jantar Mantar, staged a brief protest and waved the Tricolour before police detained them.
